px.transport: QUIC preferred with authenticated TLS fallback

xray.inner_application: HTTPS TLS with verified owned CA

config_parameters.secrets: omitted; regenerate private configs with provided scripts

notes: Every protocol uses the same fixed physical link budget; PX also has an application frame pacer.
A common source-paced background follow-up is needed to isolate generic rate-limiting gains.
Warmup runs a separate application workload; reusable proxy outer sessions persist into measurement.
All operation failures/timeouts/censoring are retained; successful-only percentiles cannot be read alone.
nstat TCP retransmission deltas include all namespace TCP sockets, including loopback proxy/fixture sockets; they do not measure QUIC retransmissions.
Resource CPU is percent of one core; guest has two vCPUs; GOMAXPROCS=1 per process.
This is a separate CC screening batch after the common-source pacing and scheduler ablations.
Stable PX is upstream quic-go v0.65.0 Reno; fork Reno controls for the older Hy QUIC fork and explicit QUIC v1.
Compare fork Reno/BBR/Brutal to isolate controller changes; stable-vs-fork changes are not solely CC gains.
No rebinding or recovery is injected here. The experimental fork can reset its controller to Reno on path migration.
Every PX trial validates QUIC attachments; experimental trials also validate both endpoints' actual post-auth controller logs.

hycc_source.transformation: Only replace the Hysteria internal congestion import-path prefix with proto-x/internal/hycc. Controller logic and constants, including upstream tests, are unchanged.

cc_provenance.fork_delta: CC installed after app authentication; explicit QUIC v1; same scheduler/session/config semantics
cc_provenance.path_migration_limitation: fork may reset CC to Reno on migration; not exercised in static-path screening
